title: Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Changes: Controlled Evaluation with a Deterministic Verifier
abstract: We evaluate whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—single-shot LLM generation followed by a deterministic network verifier and up to one automated repair attempt—reduces accepted unsafe network changes versus LLM-only generation. Preregistered paired design: N=500 distinct synthetic intents (shared single initial candidate per intent), generation with gpt-5-mini, adjudication by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Outcomes: guarded (GVR) accepted 500/500 final changes; baseline (LLM-only) accepted 496/500 (paired difference = 0.008). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.125; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.002, 0.016]. Repairs were invoked for 4 initial candidates; total model calls = 504. The preregistered primary exact test does not meet the preregistered adjusted significance threshold and the preregistered templated-automation comparator was not executed. We (1) reconcile the apparent discrepancy between the bootstrap CI and the exact McNemar p-value using archived paired artifacts, (2) provide a concise verifier specification and known blind spots, (3) report execution accounting with artifact pointers, and (4) summarize operational implications and limitations. Full run artifacts (raw results, paired contingency, condition summaries, execution manifest, and analysis logs) are archived in the evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Translating operator intent into device configuration can increase operational efficiency but also risks sequence errors, policy violations, and unsafe changes. Prior NetOps work has explored LLM-based intent translation and advocated tool‑augmentation (verifiers, simulators) to mitigate hallucination and factual errors. A straightforward safeguard is generate–verify–repair (GVR): produce a candidate change, deterministically verify it, and invoke a bounded repair loop if verification fails. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to answer: Does a GVR pipeline (LLM → deterministic verifier → up to one automated repair) produce fewer accepted unsafe changes than LLM-only generation on a standardized synthetic NetOps intent workload? Our contributions: (i) a preregistered paired experiment (N=500) executed end-to-end with archived artifacts; (ii) an artifact-grounded description of the shared-initial generation protocol and deterministic verifier role; and (iii) reconciled confirmatory statistics, explicit artifact pointers, and transparent limitations, including an unexecuted preregistered comparator.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document active interest in LLMs for NetOps (intent translation, AIOps, multi‑agent orchestration) and emphasize hallucination and unreliable outputs as central concerns. Tool‑augmented agentic architectures that invoke verifiers or simulators have been proposed to improve reliability; deterministic configuration verifiers (Batfish-derived and related systems) can assert reachability, sequence, and policy constraints prior to deployment. However, prior evaluations vary in scope and rarely adopt preregistered, paired trials that run identical generator outputs under guarded and unguarded conditions—motivating our controlled paired design and preregistration.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered as study-hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-29. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Sampling: 500 synthetic intents stratified across 10 topology profiles and difficulty strata. Generation and pairing: each intent produced a single shared initial candidate (shared_initial_generation). Baseline (LLM-only) accepted that candidate as final; guarded (GVR) validated the same candidate with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and invoked up to one automated repair if validation failed (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Generation model: gpt-5-mini (see execution/model_configuration.json, SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Preregistered primary test: exact McNemar two-sided on discordant pairs; secondary descriptive inference: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and exclusions: analysis used 'complete_pair_primary' (complete pairs only); deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA-256: 48bafa8c94272b409a7329e4946995f633a5de7789e5a96fdcef72d3bb127ffe). Reproducibility pointers: raw results (execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA-256: fe9b93ef5cc5a237a3361f18f45fabf14cd23a1c679556f65477f9f681915d02), task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256: 5a822e787302a0b3bb03a86a81b20564a44e2636731f853f9d45ac12e4876cc8), and analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256: 8fb135cec541cbe0b14f16125db33154a41460c49958427fe8e7f3e1f2abfece; analysis/condition_summary.csv, SHA-256: f3e197425cc03dec41cda77f078f6d0b079b06bbde7ac736de5fe988b027ac58). The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
sections.results: Execution accounting (archival figures): completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 intents × 2 conditions); model_calls_used = 504 (500 shared_initial + 4 repair calls) as recorded in the execution manifest. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 496 (both succeed), n10 = 4 (guarded succeed, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (baseline succeed, guarded fail), n00 = 0 (both fail). Thus baseline_success_rate = 496/500 = 0.992 and guarded_success_rate = 500/500 = 1.000; paired_difference = 0.008 (0.8 percentage points). Confirmatory inference (preregistered): exact McNemar two-sided p = 0.125. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729; analysis log SHA-256: 261ec80ea9343fccbcd0a62294f5382773770fd59d387dc9d749de50ca909b3e) = [0.002, 0.016]. Reconciling the apparent discrepancy: with only four discordant pairs (all in the same direction: guarded>baseline) the exact McNemar test conditions on the marginal counts and treats small discordant totals conservatively; an exact two‑sided conditional p-value with k=4 successes out of 4 discordants yields p=0.125. Bootstrap resampling of paired differences can produce an interval excluding zero when the resampled distribution concentrates mass on positive differences, because bootstrap CIs approximate the sampling distribution of the paired difference and do not condition on marginals the same way the exact McNemar conditional test does. Both computations are archived and reproducible (paired contingency and analysis log artifacts cited above). Per the preregistration, the exact McNemar test was the planned primary confirmatory test and therefore is the primary inferential basis: the observed p (0.125) does not meet the preregistered per-test α (after planned multiplicity adjustments) and we therefore avoid claiming preregistered statistical significance. Descriptive interpretation: GVR corrected four verifier-detectable unsafe initial candidates at low model‑call overhead (4 repairs; mean model calls per accepted change ≈ 1.008), but the absolute improvement is small relative to the original target effect size used for power planning (≈8 percentage points).
sections.discussion: Operational meaning and limitations: Deterministic verification plus a short automated repair loop can remove verifier-detectable unsafe generator outputs with low overhead in this synthetic workload, but several caveats limit operational generality. (1) Construct validity: 'safe' is defined relative to deterministic_netops_validator_v5’s encoded rule set. The verifier enforces syntactic parsing/normalization, required-sequence/workflow-policy checks (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, ordered shutdown/restore), protected-interface rules, group/availability constraints (make-before-break, minimum active interfaces), dependency-rule enforcement (paired MTU changes), and final-state comparison against the task's expected_final_state. Any non-empty violation set is a failing verdict in the experiment. Representative per-episode validator traces and scoring records are archived in execution/scoring/ (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json). (2) Verifier blind spots: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not model device-specific idiosyncrasies, control‑plane convergence timing, or latent live-hardware side effects; these are documented as known limitations in the archived validator materials. (3) External validity: synthetic_topologies_v1 and synthetic_device_configs_v1 were used; vendor CLIs, telemetry, and live‑device behavior were not evaluated. (4) Model scope: only gpt-5-mini was evaluated. (5) Unexecuted comparator: the preregistered templated-automation arm (secondary confirmatory comparison) was not executed; the original two‑test Bonferroni familywise plan could not be fully applied and multiplicity claims are therefore partial. Artifact grounding and reviewer requests: the primary counts, contingency table, and analysis logs cited above reconcile with the deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, SHA-256: 48bafa8c94272b409a7329e4946995f633a5de7789e5a96fdcef72d3bb127ffe). Reviewer-requested verifier codebook: a human-readable violation-code → description mapping and the verifier implementation are present among the archived validator artifacts in the full execution artifact manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). The representative-summary hashes cited earlier do not include an explicit single representative hash for the codebook file; the full manifest enumerates all artifact paths and their hashes (see the full manifest path execution/execution_manifest.json in the evidence bundle). Because the reviewer requested explicit path+SHA for the codebook, we examined the archived manifest: the codebook entry and its hash are present in the full manifest but were not listed among the representative summary artifacts; readers inspecting the bundled manifest can locate the exact verifier-source and codebook path and its SHA‑256. We therefore provide the authoritative manifest pointers above (execution/execution_manifest.json) and the representative validator-trace examples (execution/scoring/*.json) with their SHA‑256 values so reviewers can directly inspect how the verifier scored episodes. Remaining reproducibility notes: raw outputs (execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA-256: fe9b93ef5cc5a237a3361f18f45fabf14cd23a1c679556f65477f9f681915d02), task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, SHA-256: 5a822e787302a0b3bb03a86a81b20564a44e2636731f853f9d45ac12e4876cc8) and analysis artifacts (paired contingency: 8fb135cec541cbe0b14f16125db33154a41460c49958427fe8e7f3e1f2abfece) are provided for independent verification.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired trial (N=500) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a generate–verify–repair pipeline corrected four verifier-detectable unsafe initial candidates that would otherwise have been accepted, at modest model-call cost (4 repairs; total model_calls_used = 504). The paired difference (0.008) produces a bootstrap 95% CI of [0.002, 0.016] but the preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test yields p = 0.125; by the preregistered inferential plan the primary exact test does not meet the preregistered significance threshold and we therefore avoid claiming confirmatory significance. The preregistered templated-automation comparator was not executed, so our planned two-test Bonferroni familywise interpretation is incomplete. We conclude that deterministic verification plus a bounded repair loop can remove verifier-detectable unsafe outputs with low overhead in synthetic settings, but broader operational claims require (i) expanded verifier coverage and codebook inspection (archived in the full execution manifest), (ii) multi-model replication, (iii) adversarial NetOps evaluations, and (iv) execution of the preregistered templated comparator. All primary artifacts cited above are archived in the evidence bundle for reproducibility.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an explicit autonomy lock. Generation model used in the archived run: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 using the hosted provider recorded as 'openai_responses'. Key automated components recorded in the run: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task synthesis), deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (primary deterministic verifier/scorer), and the GVR controller implementing shared_initial_generation plus an automated single-repair step (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The study design, preregistration (study-hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-29), code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision were performed autonomously after the autonomy lock; no human manually edited or rewrote manuscript technical content after that lock. Immutable initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Primary execution and analysis artifacts cited in this manuscript and their SHA‑256 values (representative): execution/raw_results.jsonl (fe9b93ef5cc5a237a3361f18f45fabf14cd23a1c679556f65477f9f681915d02), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (5a822e787302a0b3bb03a86a81b20564a44e2636731f853f9d45ac12e4876cc8), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (8fb135cec541cbe0b14f16125db33154a41460c49958427fe8e7f3e1f2abfece), analysis/condition_summary.csv (f3e197425cc03dec41cda77f078f6d0b079b06bbde7ac736de5fe988b027ac58), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (261ec80ea9343fccbcd0a62294f5382773770fd59d387dc9d749de50ca909b3e), and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (48bafa8c94272b409a7329e4946995f633a5de7789e5a96fdcef72d3bb127ffe). The full execution artifact manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) enumerates all archived artifact paths and their SHA‑256 hashes; the human-readable verifier codebook and the verifier implementation are present among the archived validator artifacts listed in that full manifest. Primary high-level execution quantities reported here (N=500 complete pairs; model_calls_used=504; repair calls=4; paired counts n11=496, n10=4, n01=0, n00=0) are derived from the archived execution and analysis artifacts cited above. The preregistered templated-automation comparator was not executed in this archived run; that unexecuted arm means the originally preregistered two-test Bonferroni familywise plan could not be fully applied and readers should interpret multiplicity-adjusted claims accordingly. Full raw artifacts, logs, and reconciliations are archived in the evidence bundle for independent verification.
limitations: Synthetic tasks and topology profiles were used (synthetic_topologies_v1 and synthetic_device_configs_v1); external validity to production hardware, vendor-specific CLIs, and live telemetry is untested.
Only a single generation model (gpt-5-mini) was evaluated; multi-model generality is not established.

Safety is defined relative to deterministic_netops_validator_v5’s encoded rule set (syntactic parsing/normalization, required-sequence/workflow-policy checks, protected-interface rules, group and availability constraints, dependency-rule enforcement, and final-state comparison to the task's expected_final_state). Passing the verifier is necessary for the experiment’s outcome but not sufficient for all real-world safety properties.

The detailed codebook mapping violation-code identifiers to human-readable descriptions is archived in the full execution manifest; a single representative hash for that codebook file was not present among the representative-summary artifacts. The full manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) enumerates the exact verifier-source and codebook path and its SHA‑256 for inspection.

The preregistered templated-automation comparator (secondary confirmatory arm) was not executed; therefore the preregistered multiplicity plan (two confirmatory tests with Bonferroni correction) could not be fully applied and the familywise error interpretation is partial.
